messages:
olivia: quick follow-up from the office-hours Q&A — several procurement teams asked for specifics on SOC2 Type II timing, ISO 27001 mapping, and details on BYOK/HSM support for EU workloads.

 alex (PM): can we also confirm whether evidence artifacts will be tamper-evident (hashing/signatures)? buyers asked for cryptographic chain-of-custody.

 tara (Security): good call. plan: evidence bundles will include signed manifests and hash chains for critical artifacts. auditors will be able to verify timestamps + signatures. we
are working the exact format with the assessor.

 nina (Infra): on BYOK: two parallel flows being built: (A) key import for hosted EU region (customer uploads keys into our envelope KMS) and (B) HSM-backed key handles for private deployments (customer HSMs or dedicated HSM in their VPC). Phase A first.

 matt (Sales): what's the expected ETA we should put in proposals? procurement insists on month-level dates, not vague quarters.

 tara (Security): tentative dates (engineering dependent): evidence automation + signed manifests: end of June 2026; BYOK key-import beta (EU): September 2026; HSM-backed private flows (VPC/on-prem): December 2026; ISO 27001 mapping draft: mid-May 2026. note: SOC2 Type II attestation depends on evidence window and auditor schedule (likely Q1 2027 for first Type II).

 dev-platform: audit export features: per-org S3 snapshot, real-time syslog/webhook, and a "compliance archive" with optional Glacier transition. retention UI will let customers set per-org retention and archive policies. sample enable command: 

```
redwood compliance enable-export --org acme --dest s3://acme-compliance --realtime syslog://logs.acme:514 --retention 3y
```

 alex (PM): for the HSM story, are we supporting cross-account CMK usage or will keys be physically imported into our managed KMS?

 nina (Infra): initial BYOK import keeps key material customer-owned but wrapped by our envelope keys for operational use. cross-account CMK usage and key handle proxies are Phase 2. we
have audit entries for every wrap/unwrap and key usage.

 matt (Sales): export redaction question: will default exports redact PII? how do we support auditors who need raw logs?

 tara (Security): by default we redact PII in data-plane traces. auditors can request an unredacted evidence bundle via the compliance request workflow (requires DPA & auditor NDA). unredacted bundles are produced as signed artifacts and access is time-limited.

 compliance-bot: @matt created COMP-919: "Office-hours deliverables: ISO mapping + signed-evidence spec + BYOK HSM FAQ" assigned to @alex and @tara, due 2026-05-10.

 alex (PM): i'll own the ISO mapping doc and the short one-pager for sales. will ping solutions-eng for procurement phrasing.

 nina (Infra): small engineering note: we'll emit a per-key import provenance record (who/when/which-hsm) and make it part of the evidence bundle.

 tara (Security): risk note: interactive unredacted access increases surface area; mitigation = short windows, mandatory approvals, live monitoring, and an on-call approval step for high-sensitivity requests. details in workflow doc.

 matt (Sales): perfect. once the one-pager and dates are sticky we can update the procurement templates.

 olivia: thanks everyone. tara/alex please paste the key bullets into the all-hands follow-up so i can include in the customer summary email.

 tara (Security): will post a 5-bullet summary in ~1 hour and attach the ticket links. :rocket:
